issues.description: Silent semantic change from req.stream.read() to req.bounded_stream.read() smuggled into example without explanation
issues.detail: The load-bearing code change in examples/things_advanced.py line 109 swaps req.stream.read() for req.bounded_stream.read(). These are not equivalent abstractions: req.stream is the raw WSGI input (may block or over-read), while req.bounded_stream is bounded by Content-Length. The PR description misstates the change as 'add req.content_length to req.stream.read()' which does not match the diff. No comment explains why bounded_stream is the correct ADT here, leaving the precondition (admissible Content-Length values) and postcondition (behavior when Content-Length is a lie) unstated. Either fix the description or add a comment naming the invariant.

issues.description: README diff smuggles unrelated refactors and a public signature change into a test-additions PR
issues.detail: The README diff mixes cosmetic reformatting (trailing commas, line wrapping, %-format -> .format, str concat -> code_to_http_status) with a real behavioral edit: StorageError.handle(ex, req, resp, params) -> handle(req, resp, ex, params), plus the same req.stream -> req.bounded_stream swap. The signature change is a real Falcon error-handler contract change with no test, no news fragment, no rationale. Mixing semantic and cosmetic changes makes the diff hard to review and bisect. Split into separate patches: (1) the bounded_stream fix with its own justification, (2) the signature/cleanup change with its own rationale, (3) the cosmetic reformat on its own.

issues.description: FAQ example is overbuilt and teaches the wrong pattern, conflating multiple concerns
issues.detail: The new FAQ entry purports to teach how to override headers in tests, but wraps that one-line mechanism in a 30+ line PostTest resource that hand-rolls length checking against req.stream rather than using the bounded_stream ADT. The handler complects three distinct concerns: declared Content-Length, actual body bytes, and parse success, with no stated invariant for the three-branch (200/201/400) behavior. Readers will copy this pattern and inherit the conflation. Strip the example to the minimum that demonstrates simulate_post header override, document the contract explicitly, and align the stream API choice with things_advanced.py.

issues.description: Test asserts only status codes and does not actually pin the regression it claims to guard
issues.detail: resp4 sends Content-Length: 1 with empty body and asserts status_code == 400, but the example handler returns 400 for 'Empty request body' as well — the same status code an honest empty POST would produce. The test does not distinguish 'bounded_stream returned empty due to Content-Length lie' from 'body was empty and triggered the not-body branch' from 'JSON decode failure'. It would pass for the wrong reason as easily as the right one. The location and persistence postconditions of on_post (resp.location, db.add_thing) are also not verified. Assert the response title/body or the specific code path, plus the Location header on resp3.

issues.description: FAQ uses parenthesized assert that reads as a function call
issues.detail: `assert(result.status == falcon.HTTP_400)` looks like a function call but assert is a statement. The two-argument form `assert(x, y)` is the well-known antipattern that silently always passes. Since the FAQ is a teaching surface that readers will copy, write `assert result.status == falcon.HTTP_400` without parens.

issues.description: FAQ headers use list-of-tuples form inconsistent with dict form used elsewhere in the PR
issues.detail: The FAQ example constructs headers as `[('Content-Length', '1'),]` while the new tests in test_examples.py and the rest of the codebase use dicts. Two ways to specify headers in one PR's docs and tests is one too many; pick the dict form everywhere for a consistent data shape.

issues.description: FAQ handler contains redundant special-case logic (or 0 dead in the else branch)
issues.detail: PostTest checks `req.content_length in (None, 0)` and separately does `req.stream.read(req.content_length or 0)`. The `or 0` guard is dead code in the else branch because the outer if already excluded None and 0. Either eliminate the special case so it disappears, or document the invariant being protected — but don't carry both forms.

issues.description: Test uses magic Authorization value that only works because the example's auth is a stub
issues.detail: The example's AuthMiddleware._token_is_valid returns True unconditionally. The test passes any string. If anyone fixes the example's auth stub the tests silently break in a confusing way. A one-line comment in the test explaining 'auth is a stub in the example' would save future maintainers time.

issues.description: No news fragment visible in diff despite checklist claim
issues.detail: The PR checklist asserts towncrier news fragments under docs/_newsfragments/ have been added, but the diff shows no such file. Either the checklist is wrong or the fragment is missing. A behavioral change like bounded_stream warrants a news fragment.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR is presented as a narrow test-additions change but smuggles a real behavioral edit (req.stream -> req.bounded_stream in examples/things_advanced.py) plus unrelated README refactors including a public StorageError.handle signature change, with a PR description that misstates what the actual diff does. Six of six reviewers flagged the undocumented stream-API swap; all six flagged the README diff mixing cosmetic churn with semantic changes; all six flagged the FAQ example as overbuilt, conflating multiple concerns and teaching a pattern that bypasses the bounded_stream abstraction the framework provides. Three reviewers independently noted that the resp4 test asserts only a status code that the honest-empty-body path also returns, so the regression it claims to pin is not actually pinned. Recommended path: split into separate commits (bounded_stream fix with rationale and news fragment, README cleanup, tightened FAQ entry, tests that assert failure mode not just status), state the contract for each example resource, and align stream-API choice and header data shape across docs and tests.
